statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-56851 (GO-2026-6629): the golang.org/x/text/secure/precis package can panic on crafted input; fixed in golang.org/x/text v0.41.0 (https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6629, https://go.dev/issue/80112, https://go.dev/cl/793360). Inspected every published build of the alertmanager-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository: 36 builds, 0.31.1-r0 through 0.35.0-r2 (there is no 0.33.1-r4), on both x86_64 and aarch64, 72 packages, each verified against the repository index checksum. The payload of every package is two files, usr/bin/alertmanager and usr/bin/amtool: statically linked Go programs (no ELF interpreter) built for GOOS=linux with CGO_ENABLED=0. The function names the Go linker records in each binary (its function-name table) were searched, leaving out the standard library's own copies under vendor/golang.org/x/. golang.org/x/text is listed in the Go build information of both programs (v0.33.0 in 0.31.1-r0 rising to v0.44.0 in 0.35.0-r0 to 0.35.0-r2; v0.41.0 or later from 0.33.1-r5), but the only golang.org/x/text/secure package compiled into any build is bidirule. No build contains any function from golang.org/x/text/secure/precis, so none of the advisory's vulnerable symbols (the Profile and Transformer methods and nickAdditionalMapping.Transform) is present. Positive control: the same search finds runtime.main and golang.org/x/text/secure/bidirule functions in every binary, and finds golang.org/x/text/secure/precis.(*Profile).String in a stripped test program built for linux/amd64 against golang.org/x/text v0.36.0. The vulnerable code is not compiled into any build of this package.

The Go vulnerability database lists the Profile and Transformer methods and nickAdditionalMapping.Transform in golang.org/x/text/secure/precis as the vulnerable functions. Because it is built from the same source, we also read every published node-exporter package (27 versions, 1.10.2-r0 to 1.13.1-r0) in that repository on both architectures. Each of these packages holds exactly one file, /usr/bin/node_exporter, a Go program built with CGO_ENABLED=0. The reader finds runtime.main and main.main in every program. As a positive control, the same reader lists (*nickAdditionalMapping).Transform and (*Profile).NewTransformer in test programs we built for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 against golang.org/x/crypto v0.54.0 and golang.org/x/text v0.40.0 that call those packages. The flaw is in the golang.org/x/text/secure/precis package and is fixed in golang.org/x/text v0.41.0 (https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6629, https://go.dev/cl/793360, https://go.dev/issue/80112). This package is the Go 1.26 toolchain. The Go source tree it ships vendors a few golang.org/x/text packages under /usr/lib/go/src/vendor and /usr/lib/go/src/cmd/vendor. In no published build is golang.org/x/text/secure/precis among them. Checked every published golang-1.26-dev package for Debian 13 in the DHI Debian repository (1.26.4-0 to 1.26.11-18, amd64 and arm64), together with the oci-config and debug-symbol (dbgsym) packages built from the same source: none contains a golang.org/x/text/secure/precis directory or source file, and no ELF file in them (including the go and gofmt commands and the tools under /usr/lib/go/pkg/tool) contains golang.org/x/text/secure/precis code or symbols.
